summary: The design addresses real import and coupling problems, but several proposed seams cross existing behavioral boundaries: GraphIndex persistence has backend-specific semantics, ontology callers depend heavily on AQL projections, and wiki transport assembly is configuration-dependent. The main risks are creating abstractions that either leak ArangoDB concepts or silently weaken existing guarantees.

suggestions.title: Split pure GraphIndex core from framework adapters before enforcing import ceilings
suggestions.rationale: The current builder imports `GraphIndexEmbedder` and `PageIndexToolkit` at module load; those pull in FAISS, embedding registries, and `AbstractToolkit`. `extractors/loader.py` imports `parrot.stores.models`, while `graphindex/loader.py` imports `parrot.loaders` and `parrot.stores`. `graphindex/__init__.py` also eagerly imports analytics, communities, export, and signal modules. PEP 562 roots alone will not satisfy G2 or the ceilings; introduce pure local document/loader/provider protocols and keep framework adapters behind composition or compatibility modules.

suggestions.title: Define a behavioral persistence contract, not only a method Protocol
suggestions.rationale: The three implementations are not behaviorally equivalent: SQLite exposes `is_stale`, Postgres exposes temporal, hybrid, and embedding methods, and the Arango implementation uses tenant locks, soft deletes, and a commit protocol. They also differ in missing-store behavior and error handling. Specify transactionality, idempotency, ordering, missing-database behavior, and failure semantics in the base contract, then expose optional capabilities through explicit capability descriptors with conformance tests.

suggestions.title: Make one registry the only GraphIndex composition root, including null and Arango modes
suggestions.rationale: Backend selection is currently split: `factory.py` handles SQLite/Postgres, `loader.py` separately constructs ArangoDB or a null persistence, and dev-loop/wiki code constructs SQLite directly. A registry should own backend descriptors, lazy adapter loading, required configuration, and capability metadata; consumers should receive a resolved backend object and never branch on names. Include the no-op/in-memory path explicitly so loader behavior is not an undocumented fourth implementation.

suggestions.title: Replace storage-specific TenantContext fields or isolate them behind backend handles
suggestions.rationale: `TenantContext` requires `arango_db` and `pgvector_schema`, while ontology entities, relations, and `SearchViewDef` directly model Arango collections and ArangoSearch views. Authorization and entity resolution fabricate contexts with synthetic Arango names solely to call the store. A neutral tenant scope should carry tenant identity, ontology, and backend-provided handles; Arango names and view definitions should remain in the Arango adapter or a clearly marked dialect extension.

suggestions.title: Model ontology queries as typed operations plus an explicitly dialect-bound dynamic escape hatch
suggestions.rationale: The current public surface is `execute_traversal(aql=...)`; core mixin, authorization, and entity resolution compose inline AQL, while legal, procedures, and contracts do the same. `TraversalPattern.query_template` and `ResolvedIntent.aql` also explicitly store AQL. Define typed operations for the required projections, and represent dynamic queries as `{language, text, parameters, safety_policy}`. A backend without an executable/validated dialect must return a typed unsupported-capability result rather than accepting unvalidated text or pretending AQL is portable.

suggestions.title: Keep GraphIndex persistence layered over a private graph-document adapter, not the ontology public contract
suggestions.rationale: `GraphIndexPersistence` currently depends on a large Arango-shaped surface: collection creation, document queries, incident-edge lookup, soft deletion, and raw document restoration for commit revert. If the ontology contract becomes typed for application traversals, exposing these internals through it preserves the very coupling the feature is trying to remove. Give GraphIndex its own storage adapter or a lower-level document/edge transaction capability, and test the composition explicitly.

suggestions.title: Reconcile the proposed LLM Protocol with the callers that use `completion`
suggestions.rationale: `PageIndexLLMAdapter` exposes `ask`, `ask_structured`, and `ask_json`, but `OntologyIntentResolver` calls `llm.completion` directly. A protocol mirroring only the PageIndex methods will not satisfy the existing ontology path without an adapter, and structured-output/retry semantics could diverge. Define one caller-facing interface or explicit translators, and distinguish `ProviderNotAvailable` from ordinary extraction failures so the builder does not silently convert missing providers into a partial success.

suggestions.title: Move durable embedding writes behind persistence capabilities
suggestions.rationale: `GraphIndexEmbedder` accepts a pgvector DSN but its `_persist_to_pgvector` path is only a logging stub, while `PostgresPersistence` owns the real `upsert_embeddings` implementation. This makes embedding ownership backend-specific and bypasses the proposed persistence seam. The embedder should produce vectors and hot-index state; a declared persistence capability should store them, with the builder coordinating ordering and handling unavailable capabilities explicitly.

suggestions.title: Replace `pin.py`'s private SQLite path access with a formal capability or explicit SQLite-only boundary
suggestions.rationale: `parrot.knowledge.retrieval.pin` calls `SQLitePersistence._db_path` directly to inspect the files table. A backend registry cannot preserve this consumer generically unless source-coherence/staleness becomes a public capability. Either add that capability to the contract with defined semantics or make pinning explicitly SQLite-only and reject unsupported backends before opening them.

suggestions.title: Make the source collection manager an injected backend adapter
suggestions.rationale: `SourceCollectionManager` contains repeated `if self.backend == ...` branches throughout its CRUD and lookup methods, while `LLMWikiToolkit` independently selects SQLite, JSON, or Arango source handling. Moving one branch behind a registry will not remove this coupling. Extract a small source-store contract and keep source orchestration, locking, staleness, and serialization backend-neutral; register SQLite/JSON/Arango implementations separately.

suggestions.title: Build transport descriptors from the operation registry and test configuration-specific manifests
suggestions.rationale: The current MCP assembly conditionally mounts core wiki tools, structural, decisions, schema, ledger, bulk/sync, vault, and remote-proxy surfaces. A manifest must cover these axes, preserve exact names and Pydantic schemas, and guarantee that framework and SDK transports invoke the same plain operation. Generate descriptors from one operation registry and include stable schema fingerprints, conditional inclusion rules, and duplicate-name validation.

suggestions.title: Add contract and import tests that verify behavior, not only module counts
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests exercise subprocess imports and individual raw `execute_traversal` doubles, while the Postgres contract test is live-database-specific. Add a backend matrix using fake adapters plus reopen tests for SQLite/Postgres/Arango, commit apply/revert and staleness semantics, capability negotiation, typed ontology projections, dynamic-query rejection, and exact MCP manifests. Run import probes in fresh interpreters with blocked optional packages and assert forbidden module names after every target import.
